title: Putting Quantities Back Together
objective: Composing (joining two known parts) is the inverse of decomposing — given two parts, the whole can be found by joining them.
studentQuestion: If you know both parts, can you tell me the whole without counting everything again?
newIdea: Composing as the reverse of decomposing.

teaching.setup: Two separate small groups are shown (e.g. 3 and 4), not yet combined.
teaching.see: Here are two parts. What do you think the whole will be?
teaching.break: Predict the whole before combining (using counting-on if possible).
teaching.transform: Two separate parts — one combined whole — the reverse direction of the earlier splits.

check.prompt: Count the combined group to confirm the prediction.

examples.second: 5 and 2 to 7 (same whole as the primary example, different parts).
examples.transfer: Three parts joined in sequence (e.g. 2, 3, and 1).

mastery.evidence: Correctly predicts a whole from two known parts (using counting-on or a known fact) and confirms it, twice.
